name: Ferrogate CL-9 L-Train
description: The arterial rail system of Meridian 88, running elevated tracks through every district above Tier 2. The CL-9 cars are sixty years old and it shows — rattling frames, flickering displays, seats worn to bare metal. But it runs. Twenty hours a day, every eleven minutes, packed to capacity and beyond. For most of the city, the L is the only way to get anywhere that walking can't reach. The smell is a signature blend of ozone, sweat, and cheap synth-coffee.
propulsion: Electromagnetic rail, third-rail power draw from Meridian grid
speed: Average 45 km/h, peak 80 km/h between stations
range: Full loop: 94 km circuit through 47 stations
cost: Φ2 per ride, Φ45 monthly pass
autonomy: Automated with manual override capability. Ferrogate dispatch controls routing.
common_usage: Daily commute for millions. The lifeblood of the working class. Students, laborers, gig workers, and anyone who can't afford better.
story_hooks: L-train breakdowns strand thousands and create temporary communities on platforms
Certain late-night cars are known to run routes that aren't on any schedule — ghost trains to stations that don't exist on the map
